chapter_title: There is no Joy that shall remain in the World til

6.content: and fetter it in the lump

spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** There is not a single mind [GAP-1: REVIEW existing in] the state of spiritual life, standing firm amid the commingling of good and evil, for whom blessedness endures without end.

**¶2:** Not only human minds — even Divine Love and Divine Faith, the sources of all wisdom and intelligence in the heavens, [GAP-2: ...] nor are they oppressed by falsity; they know not [GAP-3: ...] established in Divine calling and in [obe]dience to Divine order. Nevertheless, even they do not attain complete blessedness.

**¶3:** So, first: Their understanding gazes upon their Adversary — the ruling evil of self-love — they [perceiv]e it and behold its monstrous persuasions. They [s]ee that it is active and entrenched and reigns over both interior and exterior states of mind, in what is hidden and in what is manifest. It accomplishes everything from its own proprium according to its own wi[GAP-4: ll].

**¶4:** [The s]econd: They perceive the Divine good implanted in humanity; they see [i]t and that it is captive and held in a great [GAP-5: REVIEW bondage of falsity] in both interior and exterior states, in perceptions and in sensual nature, [GAP-6: ...] with every form of violence against it. It is compressed, drawn toward [GAP-7: REVIEW and] severed and consumed as it passes between higher and lower states — from the interior into the exterior and from the exterior into the interior. It [GAP-8: REVIEW is] stripped of its truths and displaced from one containing form to another.

**¶5:** Now, because of the Divine good that is loved and cherished by them, when they behold it in such anguish th[ey can]not attain complete blessedness.

**¶6:** So, one grief concerning the Divine good in captivity; and another concerning their Adversary whom they perceive ruling [GAP-9: REVIEW in] what does not belong to it — self-love glorifying itself and gorged on goods and truths it has stolen. Indeed, because of this they do not rejoice wholly, but endure and contain their grief inwardly until they purify the Divine good and reclaim it from the power of evil. Then they annihilate the spiritual death that is their Adversary, and they gather all evil together [GAP-10: REVIEW and confine it in the mass of hell] to eternity.

**¶7:** When they shall confine their Adversary in that eternal bond at the [las]t, then they shall attain complete blessedness and grieve no longer from that t[ime]. And they become restored to the very same Divine order in which they existed from the [GAP-11: REVIEW beginning], unto eternity.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: There is not [o]ne person [existing in] the world, standing firm [i]n mixture, for whom joy remains to the end.

Not only people, even the sun and the moon, the light-givers of the heavens, [they do not suffer] nor are they oppressed, they know not [sorrow]et firm in a summons and an [obe]dience. Nevertheless, they too, they do not rejoice completely.

So, one: Their eyes stare at their Enemy, they [perceiv]e him and also look at his ugly shapes. They [s]ee him, that he is alive and established and is king above and below, in secret and manifest. He does every thing that he wants according to his wil[l].

[The s]econd: They perceive the living soul, they see [i]t and that it is ensnared and set in a great [fetter] above and below, in the tree and in the flesh, [afflicted] with every oppression. It is being pressed, drawn near to [and] sliced and eaten as it comes up and down; from above below and from below above. It [is] despoiled and moved from body to body.
Now, because of their living soul that is loved by them and honoured of them, when they see it in oppression th[ey can] not [re]joice completely.

So, one about the soul; and one about their Enemy whom they see ruling [in] what is not his own. He is proud and satisfied with a wealth that is not his own. Indeed, due to this, they do not rejoice in total; but bear up and swallow their heart until they cleanse the living soul and take it from the Enemy's hands. Then they obliterate the Death that is their Enemy and they gather it in [and fetter it in the lump] for ever and ever.
When they will chain their Enemy in the bond at the [las]t, then they will rejoice and no longer grieve from this t[ime]. Also, they become the very same as they were from the [beginning] for ever!

fills.explanation: The editor's "existing in" correctly conveys the sense of a person dwelling/present in the world amid the state of mixture, matching the spiritual reading's "existing in the state of spiritual life."

The passage establishes a tricolon of negatives about the sun and moon (they do not suffer / nor are they oppressed / they know not affliction) before the concessive "Nevertheless" — they are personally free from suffering yet still cannot fully rejoice due to witnessing the soul's captivity.

The sun and moon "know not sorrow" completes the tricolon of negatives describing their personal freedom from affliction, before the participial clause "set firm in a summons and obedience" explains why — they are established in Divine calling.
The word is "will" — the Enemy does everything "according to his will," with only the final letter missing from the damaged manuscript edge.

The editor's "fetter" is confirmed — the living soul is "ensnared and set in a great fetter," corresponding to the spiritual sense of bondage/captivity, and "fetter" is standard Kephalaia vocabulary for the soul's imprisonment in matter.

The soul is "afflicted with every oppression" — the spiritual reading indicates "every form of violence against it," and "afflicted" naturally governs the prepositional phrase "with every oppression" describing the soul's torment in tree and flesh.
The editor's "and" is confirmed — it continues the list of violent actions upon the soul: pressed, drawn near, and sliced and eaten, matching the spiritual reading's parallel construction.
The editor's "is" is confirmed as the copula — "It is despoiled and moved from body to body" describes the ongoing passive state of the soul being stripped and displaced.

The editor's "in" is confirmed — the Enemy is "ruling in what is not his own," meaning exercising dominion over a domain that does not belong to it, corresponding to self-love usurping goods and truths.

fills.fill: and fetter it in the lump
fills.original: and fetter it in the lump
fills.explanation: The editor's phrase is confirmed — "the lump" (bolos) is the standard Manichaean term for the final mass in which all evil/darkness is permanently confined, corresponding to Swedenborg's hell as a confined globus; "fetter" matches the permanent confinement described in the spiritual reading.

Correcting "start" to "beginning" — in the Kephalaia's cosmological register, "beginning" (Coptic ⲁⲣⲭⲏ) is the standard term for the primordial state before mixture, corresponding to the original Divine order that is restored at the end of the age.
